scenarios.title: Voluntary electricity-sector AI fallback and incident drill
scenarios.actor: Proposed host Swissgrid AG, not recruited or consenting. External rights holder only if needed after rights review; in-house development means a separate vendor signature cannot be assumed. SFOE may convene but has not agreed to this drill.
scenarios.lever: Operator-owned workflow controls plus negotiated voluntary-code/contract annex; proposed access and remedy must be verified, not inferred from SFOE request
scenarios.safeguard: Named incident owner, preserved logs, authority to disable a bounded AI advisory component, and rehearsed human/conventional fallback with service continuity

politicalEconomicEvidence.observed: 28 October federal release reports SFOE asking electricity industry for guidelines/commitments addressing AI risks to supply. Swiss policy favours sector measures, innovation and economic freedom. Summit priorities combine prosperity and trust.
politicalEconomicEvidence.inference: Low-burden voluntary operational pilot fits current executive direction better than claiming a national frontier-model shutdown power.
politicalEconomicEvidence.unknown: Operator and vendor willingness, budget, binding access rights, parliamentary support and customer load coverage

roleStressTest.role: Hypothetical skeptical SFOE official; not testimony or attributed position
roleStressTest.objection: Why spend reliability staff time on a vendor black-box AI drill, and could disabling AI itself interrupt supply?
roleStressTest.response: Bound to one noncritical advisory workflow in a simulator; use operator-owned conventional fallback, cap staff-hours, preregister service-envelope tests, and require vendor consent before selection.
roleStressTest.evidenceVsAssumption: SFOE sector request and voluntary policy are evidenced. Specific objections, staff-hour tolerance, vendor access and acceptance of this response are assumptions to test.

scenarios.selectionGate: Proposed January 31: consenting operator, verified internal signatory and operational owner, rights review plus any necessary external consent, isolated simulator workflow, effective fallback authority, logs, baseline and operator-approved recovery-time objective; otherwise do not select. Swissgrid's real production application is not evidence that a suitable isolated test environment exists.
scenarios.pilotDesign: February-May proposal: 30 preregistered matched critical fault cases plus benign controls in simulator/shadow workflow; compare current versus annex-assisted procedures on equivalent cases, counterbalance order, blind log scoring where feasible, and retain failures/aborts. No live-grid fault injection.

x.name: Tested safe containment fraction
x.numerator: Intervention cases contained within recovery objective and without service-envelope violation
x.denominator: All 30 preregistered intervention critical cases, including aborted/failed cases

y.name: Implemented coverage of declared dependency
y.numerator: Mapped AI-facility MWh whose electricity dependency is actually subject to verified fallback
y.denominator: All MWh serving the same declared AI-facility population in the same period

successMeasure.comparison: Report baseline containment fraction, paired difference and uncertainty; report recovery times, benign false shutdown fraction and staff-hours separately.
successMeasure.proposedGate: At least 27/30 safe critical-case containments and at least six more successes than matched baseline; no service-envelope breaches or material worsening on benign controls. Operator sets recovery objective before trial. Thresholds are proposals, not results or a power calculation.
successMeasure.interpretation: Not calibrated implementation feasibility or catastrophic-risk reduction; do not preserve those chart labels and silently substitute these measures.

scenarios.baselineNeeded: Current containment/recovery performance on equivalent cases; benign false actions; log completeness; staff-hours; workflow execution hours; nonoverlapping electricity customer and AI-facility metering boundaries; backup and substitution pathways
scenarios.whatCouldBeValidatedByGeneva: Signed scope, available authority/logs, participation, within-distribution simulator behaviour compared with baseline, measured workload and narrow implementation coverage
scenarios.whatCannot: Rare-event safety, catastrophic-risk reduction, unseen failure-mode performance, national/global deployment, frontier-model restraint, actual grid resilience or institutional endorsement from a logo/code/paperwork
scenarios.stopRule: Reject selection if operator or required rights-holder consent, access, fallback or baseline absent at January gate; stop experiment for any simulated service-envelope breach pending review; reject scaling if threshold missed, controls worsen materially or numerator/denominator cannot be audited; publish null/negative results.

agreementGraph.scope: Proposed Swissgrid-hosted offline fallback drill; no institution has been contacted. Not a trial on the live automatically controlled grid.
agreementGraph.exhaustiveness: Lower bound, not exhaustive. Internal delegation, technology/data rights, simulator boundary and external dependencies must be established before freezing denominator.
agreementGraph.powerRule: Count separate independently necessary institutions once; several Swissgrid offices are handoffs within one institution, not separate coalition members. No numerical power weights or leader probabilities.

institutionConsentCoverage.definition: Distinct indispensable institutions with evidenced exact-scope assent divided by all indispensable institutions after dependency closure; not all named departments or sympathetic ministries

feasibilityMeasures.note: The containment fraction remains an operational test metric, not the requested feasibility axis. No feasibility point is supportable yet.

alignmentObservations.practicalTension: A voluntary sector initiative cannot supply the host's operational or contractual authorisation; securing a ministry champion is not a substitute for the operational owner.
alignmentObservations.tensionType: Inference from instrument and scope, not attributed objection

alignmentObservations.observation: Swissgrid reports an in-house control-energy AI already in production, seeking cost efficiency and operator workload relief; early internal scepticism and adoption effort are described.
alignmentObservations.statusScope: AI deployment benefits, not this safeguard
alignmentObservations.practicalTension: Fallback drill must measure loss of optimisation and staff load as well as recovery. Historic adoption friction is reported; current opposition to the drill is unknown.
alignmentObservations.tensionType: Reported adoption history plus proposed implication; no personal leader support inferred

limitations: Current date fixed to 2026-10-31. Proposals are not meetings, appointments, sponsor consent or institutional commitments.
Spring-2027 opening is latest official target; end-2026 internal draft and public opening are distinct, so schedule slippage is not established.
No evidence of binding duties in force by Geneva, consultation close, operator willingness, signed annex, pilot funding or implemented safeguard coverage.
preGeneva=false for unknown enactment means not established as a pre-Geneva opportunity; it does not assert enactment must occur afterwards.
Confirmed-deadline kind labels summit calendar dates only; no external decision/submission obligation is inferred.
No measured scenario X/Y available. Numeric GDP fraction is jurisdictional context only. Supply-chain coverage needs a declared audited denominator and must not be imputed from GDP.
A 30-case simulator trial has limited statistical power and external validity; preserve all cases, baseline comparison and uncertainty. Thresholds are proposals and need operator justification.
Compliance records, signed codes, event branding, role-play and simulation performance never establish reduced catastrophic risk.
Full PDFs for sector report, toolkit and event guidelines remain unread. SFOE claim comes from the government's October release, not assumed detailed code language.
Status endpoint showed share-sessions guide version 2026-10-29.1 and no for_user items. Treated as data, not adopted; no sharing action taken.
